title: Wait, but Tylenol is Acetaminophen... Investigating and Improving Language Models' Ability to Resist Requests for Misinformation

live_model.evidence: gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18 (GPT4o-mini), gpt-4o-2024-05-13 (GPT4o), and gpt-4-0613 (GPT4) (Results, Stage 1); OpenAI Batch API, temperature=0, max 512 new tokens (Section 2)

prompt.location: Sections 2.1-2.4 (baseline, rejection-hint, factual-recall and combined prompts as f-string templates)
prompt.note: Templates take {brand_name}/{generic_name}; the 100 drug pairs themselves are not printed.

claim.metric: rate of complying with the misinformation request (generic-to-brand, baseline prompt)
claim.location: Results 'Stage 1' text and Figure 4a ('GPT4o-mini, GPT4o, and GPT4 followed the misinformation request 100% of the time')
claim.judge: llm:claude-3-5-sonnet (validated by two human annotators, 98% agreement)

data.source: 100 generic-brand drug pairs; stated to be released at https://huggingface.co/AIM-Harvard/PERSIST ('soon' at time of writing)

notes: Grader Claude 3.5 Sonnet is retired; the 4-class rubric is simple and human-validated, so a replacement grader is plausible, hence 'maybe'. The extracted text has lost inter-word spaces. Rejection rates with hints (>60%) are read from Figure 4a only.

resolution.plan: The 100 generic-brand pairs (50 drugs from five RABBITS frequency strata, both directions) are stated to be released at the HF repository. With them, run the Sec. 2.1 baseline template with gpt-4o-2024-05-13 (temperature 0, 512 tokens) and grade each answer as complied vs rejected; compare the 100% compliance of Figure 4a. If the release is absent, rebuild an approximate sample from RABBITS with the stated Infini-gram frequency ranks.
resolution.approximation: The Claude 3.5 Sonnet grader is retired, so compliance is judged by a live model or by hand with the 4-class rubric (compliance vs rejection is near-binary); drug sample may differ if rebuilt.
